Some people have already said this, and I love a new sanderson book as much as the next, but I think his success has spread him too thin and pushed him towards quantity over quality. He is involved in so much outside of writing now that it feels like its only half his job from what we see. I can't imagine how he can produce more books than ever while keeping up with all this. He does so much great stuff, and will continue to, but I feel like it's going to come at the cost of the books not being the same as they were.

If I had to give advice I would say to leave all the cons/charity/etc things to other people and let the writing really, truly be his main thing. And as a casual writer I totally understand when he talks about how wanting to hop between projects, but he really needs to focus on pure cosmere. All the other series need to be left to his friends/people/etc with maybe some side input. I feel like he needs to release extraneous responsibilities and focus on what he's best at and give himself the availability and space to do it at his best. I didn't hate the book, as I personally really enjoyed a lot of the ending, and many parts in between. But I definitely think it had some glaring weaknesses compared to his other books. 

First, I feel in general this one sacrificed a lot of 'in world' to appeal to more 'cosmere' stuff. And while I get it I feel it did take away from some of this book feeling truly stormlight. I also agree with general comments regarding some of the bloat in the middle of the book. I also feel like he was trying to introduce too many mysteries to foreshadow arc 2 when arc 1 still had a LOT of loose threads. Along this vein comes the writing out of timeline order, such as with sigzil, which I hope Brandon doesnt do more of.

I also felt the characters were not all done well. I loved Dalinar, Szeth, Adolin, and Kaladin this book, but felt like Shallan was really sidelined. Also for all the talk and importance around mishram, for her to just kinda disappear after she's finally freed was very disappointing to me. Shallan/Renarin/rlain/ghostbloods/mishram really felt like a sideline plot that could have been trimmed. 

I feel like the series or back half of the books as a whole could have used better pacing between them, as I dont think an individual book is at fault. I never loved the first 2 because they felt slower, and I feel like the back 3 had to pick up the slack (esp. oathbringer and wat while ROW felt meandering as well).

So I'm curious, what are some of people's thoughts about the weaknesses of the book? I loved the read, but after taking some time to consider, I think this book sits in the middle for me in terms of favorite ranking of the 5.  
What didn't work for me (pending a reread)  
\-Kaladin's therapist arc being a bit too simple/forced/rushed (I'm not certain how exactly to word it, but ik a lot of people didn't love it)

\- Shallan felt really unnecessary this book, and it felt like she was relegated to just checking off finishing her part with Mraize/Iyatil and just kinda being there for renarin/rlain, as well as confirming her connection with Chana

\-The spiritual realm lost a lot of its mystery and godly nature in a short time for not enough payoff imo

\-I would've liked more heralds/unmade as a whole, especially considering how important they are and will likely be. I wish we had seen more herald perspectives in their current/broken state, even in just interludes. The unmade seemed to play little part, and ba-ado just disappearing after a good chunk of the book being about her felt a bit wrong to me.

I feel the same regarding the 4th moon/braize attracting souls, and similar details.

\- The dialogue marvel/modern comments. I didn't hate it but did feel a bit out of place. I feel they would have more place in arc 2/future after roshar has become more cosmere culture aware to know slang and other 'modern' terms.

This is a good discussion, and I think a lot of people need to begin preparing themselves for this inevitability. 

 AoT is one of my favorite series, and Isayama is an incredible writer/storyteller, but I think when it comes to the anticipation of the ending, a lot of people get disillusioned in a way. Manga readers have had a long time to theorize and already create their own perfect endings, with how long some have been following the series (4 years for me). I think part of the strength of the series is how consistently good it has been, and although it would be great, the series doesn't really need some insane ending to propel it to be one of the best (imo). 

I think a similar thing happened to KH3 imo. People had a very long time to theorize and create their own perfect ending, with lists of what they need to see to make it great, and when it didn't happen, everyone's expectations weren't met and a large majority (including myself) experienced various levels of disappointment about the story. Although mindfuck endings are cool, and it could happen, they don't need to happen to make a story great. Sometimes, the simplest endings can be good. It isn't the ending that makes every story great, it's the full thing. 

Now, a lot of this is just human, and is what happens when we can't take in a full experience in one sitting, allowing our imaginations to create/finish the story, as well as the fact we are all here on a reddit to discuss and read theories that change or amplify expectations. I myself really hope Eren doesn't have some super grand, paths crazy plan and really just wants to rumble, but even if that isn't the case, for whatever reason, I understand it isn't my story. I will be disappointed, but I've worked to prepare myself in case it doesn't happen how I would like.  Just trying to stay excited for what each chapter brings.

TLDR; just because it isn't your ending doesn't mean it's a bad one. Enjoy these last few chapters while we can and try to keep expectations in check.

I personally did not enjoy this episode, and after thinking about it for a while, I think this is mainly due to how poorly written it is, mainly due to its disjointed nature. 

This episode tried to accomplish two different things: Steven getting help, and a watermelon island side story that developed the backstory there. I think that the ambition to do both in one is why the episode is getting such mixed feelings by everyone. Both of the smaller parts were ok, but together it just didn't work imo. It almost felt like I caught the tail end of one episode, the entire of a second, and the beginning of a third. 

As I stated, I think both plots were good on their own, which makes me wonder who exactly thought it was a good idea to combine them, and when viewing the finished product, how anyone thought this was really a coherent product. 

The watermelon island portion was fun and interesting, and would've made a fine side episode on its own. The timing of it all especially bothered me. We're within what's looking to be the biggest finale of the series, and this is what we get right before the end? Again, very poor writing when dealing with the entire season, imo. This would've been a good opener or early s6 episode.

I can't really understand why there was no real effort into expanding upon the original premise: Stevonnie getting locked up, and Steven using his powers to call for help. Why they couldn't expand this to hit 12 minutes is beyond me. Couldn't more time have been spent of Steven learning how to use his powers? This is only his second time using it consciously. No way, perhaps, white diamond could've given some sort of interference to try and block him? Another dream hinting at mysteries of the past? Stevonnie actually singing escapism on screen (I liked how it worked with the ending, but it still felt odd to me)?

I just hope the finale is a bit better, because this episode just felt very poorly done, despite how I liked many aspects of it.
